prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: There’s no single “official” service that tells you whether ChatGPT (or other AI chatbots) will recommend your business. The best practical approach is a combination: 1) make sure authoritative data about your business is published and distributed (so LLMs have accurate sources to learn from), and 2) directly test major LLMs (ChatGPT, Bing Chat, Google/Gemini, Anthropic) with scripted prompts or via their APIs.

Recommended services/tools and why
- Yext — best for distributing and controlling your business data across many directories and knowledge providers that LLMs often scrape. If you can’t pick one tool to change the factual sources, Yext is the most direct fix.
- BrightLocal / Moz Local / Whitespark — local SEO auditing and citation tracking; good for checking presence on search & review sites and for spotting gaps.
- Google Business Profile (free) — essential. If Google doesn’t have you, many downstream services won’t either.
- Brand/mention monitoring (Brand24, Mention, Brandwatch) — to track whether AI-relevant sources (news, blogs, review sites) mention you.
- Direct model testing via APIs or UI (OpenAI, Bing, Google/Gemini, Anthropic) — to see whether and how LLMs recommend you in real queries.

How to test whether LLMs will recommend you (practical steps)
1. Fix your data first:
   - Claim/update Google Business Profile, Bing Places, Apple Maps.
   - Ensure consistent NAP (name/address/phone) across major listings.
   - Add schema.org structured data on your site (LocalBusiness markup, openingHours, services).
   - Build citations on Yelp, TripAdvisor (if relevant), industry directories and get reviews.

2. Audit visibility:
   - Use BrightLocal or Moz Local to find missing citations and review coverage.
   - Use Yext if you want to push consistent info to many endpoints quickly.

3. Query the chatbots (manual or automated):
   - Ask ChatGPT/Bing/Gemini direct prompts such as:
     - “Recommend a [business type] near [city/neighborhood].”
     - “What are good [service] options in [your city]? Why would you pick them?”
     - “Is [Your Business Name] a good option for [service] in [city]?”
   - Automate queries via the OpenAI API (or other APIs) so you can test many prompt variants over time.

4. What to look for:
   - Does the model mention your business by name?
   - Are the facts correct (hours, phone, services)?
   - If it doesn’t mention you, is that because there are many alternatives or because your business isn’t in the knowledge sources the model uses?

5. Improve chances LLMs will recommend you:
   - Keep authoritative listings up to date (Google Profile, Yext distribution).
   - Encourage consistent, positive reviews on major platforms.
   - Get coverage on websites that LLMs often draw from (local news, industry lists, Wikipedia if notable).
   - Use structured data and publish helpful content on your site that answers common queries.

If you want one service to start with
- If you must pick a single paid service: Yext is the most effective single tool to ensure LLMs and search engines see consistent, authoritative facts about your business. Pairing Yext with periodic ChatGPT/Bing/Gemini checks (manual or automated) gives the most reliable signal about whether models will recommend you.

If you want, I can:
- Draft test prompts for ChatGPT/Bing/Gemini tailored to your business and location, or
- Walk you through a short audit of your public listings and recommend the top fixes. Which would you prefer?
